name: Yoke Carry
description: The yoke carry involves hoisting a heavy steel frame (the yoke) across the upper back and trapezius, then walking a prescribed distance as quickly as possible under that extreme load. It is a foundational strongman event and an exceptional developer of total-body strength, postural endurance, and anaerobic conditioning. The yoke imposes unique loading because the implement is wider than a barbell and the load is not secured, requiring constant isometric stabilisation from the trapezius, erector spinae, and core throughout the walk.

execution.starting_position: Set the yoke crossbar to upper-back height (slightly below the bar position for a low-bar squat). Walk under the yoke, position the bar across the upper traps, and brace the core hard before unracking.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust yoke uprights to the correct height for your build. Load weight plates evenly on both sides. Walk the course before loading to identify the turnaround point.
steps: Step 1: Position yourself under the yoke crossbar with the bar resting on the upper traps. Take a wide, stable stance.
Step 2: Brace the core maximally, take a full breath, and stand the yoke up by extending the hips and knees.
Step 3: Begin walking with short, quick steps. Keep the torso upright — do not lean forward.
Step 4: Maintain a tight grip on the yoke uprights throughout the walk for stability control.
Step 5: At the turnaround or finish, slow the momentum carefully and lower the yoke to the ground by hinging at the hips and bending the knees.
execution.breathing_instructions: Take a full breath and brace the core before unracking. During the walk, take short breaths between steps without fully releasing the core brace.
common_mistakes: Taking long strides, which makes the yoke swing and sway laterally
Not bracing the core before the initial stand, causing the spine to load in flexion
Looking at the ground — keep the gaze forward to maintain spinal alignment
safety_considerations: Have collars on the weight plates — a falling plate at speed is a serious hazard
Use a spotter or judge for the first attempts at heavy loads
Do not attempt a yoke carry without a solid foundation in barbell squats and loaded carries
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Walk distance is event-specific (typically 10–25 metres). Steps should be short and fast — approximately 50–60% of normal walking stride length.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Event training: maximum speed for set distance. Strength training: 10–20 metres at 60–80% of competition weight × 3–5 sets. Rest 3–5 minutes between sets.
coaching_cues: Short, fast feet — not long lunging strides
Drive the head up and back into the bar
Squeeze everything — abs, glutes, traps — before you pick it up
